correctness.rationale: The mixed-boundary backward differential equations uniquely determine the first two conditional moments. Repeated integration and Gaussian averaging yield exact positive compact-domain integrals. Each high-noise exponent has a unique sharp corner with two or four independent linear distances; dominated rescaling yields the reported prefactors. Exponentially tilted conditional velocities are exactly Gaussian about the spatial sum, and corner localization proves their limiting centering. The standard renewal identity and finite second moment give the small-reset slope, while a Gaussian/Brownian small-time bound ensures the mean restarted time diverges at large reset rate; hence a nonzero global minimizer exists when the slope is negative. The zero-propulsion polynomial and sign boundary were checked algebraically. Numerical 45-test checker passed; it is not the proof.

value.rationale: The model is a natural quenched-persistence boundary of active search with both thermal noise and regenerated propulsion. Its exact exponential asymptotics show that the mean is set by exponentially rare outward velocities, while the second moment is even more singular and changes the optimal restart decision. The critical passive starting-position boundary and conditional velocity laws identify which rare paths cause the reversal and provide quantitative benchmarks for persistence/renewal studies. It is not merely a routine reparameterization of the universal reset criterion.
